Calls for better reading and math programs and points to F-rated schools in the district. Says schools are teaching 'doctrines' instead of core subjects like English, math and science.

Says he has written 11 bills to introduce if elected, including veterans-related legislation. Said he was undecided on the Major Richard Star Act and the Take Care of America's Veterans Act until he could review where the funding goes.

Would support or introduce War Powers Resolutions requiring Congress to approve further military action. Would use appropriations to withhold money for unauthorized operations, and would back bipartisan legislation barring funds to occupy or annex Greenland.

ri-united-states-senator-raymond-mckay.name: Raymond McKay
ri-united-states-senator-raymond-mckay.summary: Raymond "Ray" McKay is a Republican from Providence, Rhode Island, a former member of the Rhode Island Republican Party State Central Committee and a former president of the Rhode Island Republican Assembly. He ran for U.S. Senate in 2024 and ran again in 2026, when he was unopposed in the September 2026 Republican primary. He faces Democratic incumbent Jack Reed and independent Michael Bahry in the November 3, 2026 general election.

positions.stance: Supports American energy independence and bipartisan work for the long-term strength and stability of the nuclear and fossil fuel industries, while using green energy solutions efficiently.
Names high heating, electricity and food costs and low business investment as Rhode Island concerns. Argues that federal energy policies backed by Sen. Reed raised utility bills and hurt fishermen.
Proposes protecting Social Security and Medicare by balancing the budget, cutting wasteful and redundant spending and some programs, and prosecuting fraud.
Pledges to oppose bills he says violate the Constitution or limit personal and parental freedoms or free markets, and to seek repeal of such laws already passed.
Supports securing the borders and immigration and enforcement policies that he says put the interests of Rhode Islanders and Americans first.
In a Ballotpedia survey, said he supports school choice, including vouchers, tax credits, charter schools, private schools and homeschooling.
In an iVoterGuide questionnaire, said abortion providers, including Planned Parenthood, should not receive taxpayer funds, including Title X grants.

sd-united-states-senator-mike-rounds.occupation: U.S. Senator from South Dakota (incumbent); former insurance and real estate business owner
sd-united-states-senator-mike-rounds.summary: Mike Rounds is a Republican who has represented South Dakota in the U.S. Senate since 2015. Before that he was a state senator and served two terms as South Dakota's 31st governor (2003–2011). He announced a bid for a third Senate term in January 2026, won the Republican primary against Justin McNeal, and faces independent Brian Bengs in the November 3, 2026 general election.

positions.stance: Supports continued U.S. development of AI. He argues that China, Russia and Iran are developing it, and he is concerned about those nations getting ahead of the United States.
Supports eliminating the U.S. Department of Education and favors local control of schools. He says a federal 'one size fits all' approach does not serve students.
Describes himself as pro-life. As governor he signed a trigger law that took effect after Roe v. Wade was overturned and bans abortion in South Dakota except when the mother's life is at risk.
Supports an 'all-of-the-above' energy approach and more domestic production. Opposes what he calls excessive federal regulation of energy producers.
Says border security is essential to national security. Has supported funding for a border wall, surveillance technology and more personnel to stop drug and human trafficking.
Says he strongly supports the Second Amendment and works to protect the rights of law-abiding gun owners. He holds an A+ rating from the NRA Political Victory Fund.
Serves on the Senate Armed Services Committee and says he works to keep the U.S. military the best in the world. Cites Reagan's 'peace through strength' principle.
Cites tax cuts that he says 'put more money back in your pocket' as a Senate accomplishment and lists keeping taxes low as a priority.

sc-u-s-senate-annie-andrews.name: Annie Andrews
sc-u-s-senate-annie-andrews.summary: Annie Andrews is a pediatrician from Mount Pleasant, South Carolina, who worked about 15 years at the children's hospital of the Medical University of South Carolina (MUSC). She ran for the U.S. House in South Carolina's 1st District in 2022, lost to Rep. Nancy Mace, and announced her U.S. Senate campaign on May 29, 2025. She won the Democratic primary in June 2026 and faces Sen. Darline Graham (R), who was appointed to the seat after Sen. Lindsey Graham died.

positions.stance: Says health care is a right, not a privilege. Supports a public insurance option, reversing federal Medicaid cuts, restoring the enhanced ACA tax credits, and having South Carolina expand Medicaid.

Proposes expanding Medicare drug price negotiation, banning 'pay for delay' deals with generic drug makers, tightening rules on pharmacy benefit managers, and capping insulin out-of-pocket costs in private insurance.
Proposes ending prior authorization for routine and emergency care, banning private equity ownership of hospitals, more oversight of hospital mergers, and limits on Medicare Advantage upcoding.
Supports legislation to create criminal liability for executives she says misled the public about opioid addiction risks.
Says expanding the child tax credit and making it permanent would be one of her legislative priorities.
Says she will work to restore the protections of Roe v. Wade.
Supports universal background checks and banning what she calls weapons of war. Says she has no interest in taking guns from law-abiding citizens. Endorsed by GIFFORDS.
Released an October 2026 TV ad stating 'No men in women's sports.'
